author: [AEP] Dez [AEP]
content: "As some of our members dedicated to the lore have already figured out, the Ustur names are actually composed of two different words. The first name comes as a derivation of a collective noun, often linked in some way to the Ustur in some way, so, for an example of a first name, you could use the collective noun army and make variations of it, like Arm, Arny, and etc. The second name, though, is the most important for the Ustur society. The second name goes on this crescent order:  1) .bod 2). iddt 3). lrnr 4). doer 5). tcher 6). soul 7). eldr   Those names are linked in lore with certain milestones that, once reached, allow the Ustur to go to the next stage in the path of enlightenment.

content: Play testers should be chosen based of intrinsic value as a tester, and desire to help our economy grow and become more sustainable. (Not based on “perceived interest in sage labs, the amount of questions they asked, how involved they are, or their personality type”)   For example people should be chosen based on their knowledge of economics, how to make a game fun to play, how to hack and test the smart contract for potential vulnerabilities, or the front end to test for potential ui advantages that might break the game, those who are able to think like a bot and can help quantify/calibrate and mitigate the advantages to bots, those who are leaders of large guilds who can help calibrate how resource movement might look when dealing with multiple payers working together. Maybe social media influencers who can post some of what they see to the community (or at least have in depth videos ready for the release), or spreadsheet wizards to start creating spreadsheets that will be quickly made available to the public apon release.   If each of the playtesters had been chosen based on these merits I think we would have seen less complaints overall. And more value to the team and the community from the playtesters

author: [AEP] Steve WoodyMUD
content:
Ok So I'm going to decompress my thoughts after recording some videos. 

I currently have two accounts running. My main account (a respectful $2,500 investment in ships running 70k cargo) and (a basic entry $20 investment running 700 cargo)

The Loops are night and day in terms of what I can do and it makes me think about games I've worked with in the past and books I've read on game design and game theory. 

A game should be hard enough that you feel pain but not too much pain that you quit. The perfect balance is in making you appreciate the better things because of the initial grind. 

For this to work there has to be a sense of progression. New players that can see a path, even if painful will follow it as long as they can see an outcome.

Taking the smaller account into consideration, I would fully expect it to be much harder and much longer to get starter than someone coming in with a bigger investment but there has to be hope and a clear path. 

Having tried to mine and also scanning SDU I can say that there is no way at all that anyone will stay scanning, it's at best a 20% ROI on time and resources and just far far too painful for anyone to want to sit clicking buttons. Therefore the feeling of competing with bots and ones own thoughts about boredom and loosing sight of progression is one that could drive away initial players, also noone wants to live in google sheets or companion apps, there needs to be a feedback loop inside the game that does not require a maths degree for a new player to see potential and a clear path forward. 

I 100% respect this is a first pass, these things will take time and we are early for this - I have no doubt these things will come in time, I'm just sharing my feedback as someone who has been through this process. 

Mining and crafting will feel more fun and a lots better as a game loop for new players but thats something that is almost impossible as someone with only an airbike - 250 cargo is not even enough to get to where you need to be and then you don't have the space to move resources back and forth, this means you are almost locked to your CSS, I think there needs to at the very least be a loaner basic cargo ship that people can pay a fee (burnt atlas) to rent that allows them to see a path to owning another bike or even something like a Maxhog

It's just very unclear how anyone right now with the basic asset could find a way to progress and that has to be key in the FTUE

author: Sammy | stegaBOB [SKR]
content:
(long and potentially confusing explanation... sorry) This is more a consequence of how transaction simulations (and phantom's implementation of auto approve) work under the hood. In order to not force yall to click the wallet pop up a million times, we send batches of transactions to the wallet to sign at once (signAllTransactions). Some of the transactions depend on prior transactions to actually work; we handle the send order on our end after the wallet signs. Transaction simulations are actually an api call built directly in to rpc nodes. When you simulate a transaction, you're effectively sending a single (usually unsigned) transaction to the rpc node and telling it to simulate the transaction. Internally, the rpc node will run that transaction on the latest state of the ledger and send back the results of that to the wallet. As its currently designed, transaction simulations can't actually simulate batches together, so it will simulate all of the transactions independently, regardless of whether they are supposed to be processed in sequence together. 

One example of this would be for the following two transactions: the first creates an account, and the second closes that account. On our end, we would have the wallet sign both together and only send the second one after the first transaction is confirmed. The wallet will see both of the transactions and send multiple simulate transaction RPC calls to an RPC node. The simulation for the second transaction will fail because it thinks its trying to close an account that doesn't yet exist, even though we know that by the time we actually send that transaction, the first transaction which creates that account will have already gone through. 

As for why phantom's auto approve fails, right now if it sees one of the simulations failing it will prevent auto sign from working. So.... it breaks a lot of stuff
